articles.headline: Stunt Coordinator Geeta Tandon Alleges Disrespect On Set
articles.dek: Bollywood stunt director and body double Geeta Tandon speaks out after enduring a nine-hour wait on the set of Anil Kapoor's reality show, prompting apologies from the host and guest Farah Khan.

p: Prominent Bollywood stunt coordinator and body double Geeta Tandon recently brought public attention to an unpleasant experience she faced during a shoot. The industry professional took to social media to voice her grievances regarding how she and her son were treated behind the scenes of a high-profile television production.

The incident centers around the television project hosted by renowned actor Anil Kapoor. Tandon detailed her grievances online, emphasizing that basic human decency should never be compromised regardless of a person's standing within the entertainment business.

According to Tandon's public statement, she arrived at the designated shooting location at approximately 12:30 pm. The production team had assured her that her scheduled segment would be recorded after a brief passage of time, but this initial estimate stretched into a nearly all-day ordeal.

She noted that she and her son were confined to a tent for the duration of the delay without receiving any clear updates. Tandon had rearranged her own professional timetable and had even arranged for her son to travel back from Goa specifically to participate in the filming.

As the hours ticked by without progress, Tandon attempted to communicate with the crew members to find out when their work would begin. Instead of receiving transparency, she reported being brushed off repeatedly by staff who offered no concrete timeline for the shoot.

The situation escalated when she directly questioned a production manager named Jaydeep about the poor communication and prolonged confinement. According to her account, the response from the production side was dismissive, telling them they could leave only if they signed certain documents first.

Finding the attitude of the production crew unacceptable, Tandon and her son ultimately decided to walk away from the set at 9:15 pm. They had spent nearly nine hours waiting without receiving the courtesy of timely updates or basic hospitality.

In her social media post, she stressed that she had attended purely by invitation and had not requested any financial favors or special treatment. Her primary demand was simple professional courtesy and human dignity for everyone involved in media productions.

body.h: Reactions From Anil Kapoor And Farah Khan
p: Following the widespread attention generated by Tandon's post, key figures associated with the production stepped forward to address the matter. Host Anil Kapoor responded in the comment section to express sincere regret over the oversight during his show.

Filmmaker Farah Khan, who appeared as a guest on that particular episode, also offered an apology. Khan explained that she had been shooting for a different segment in the evening and would gladly have accommodated Tandon in her vanity van had she been aware of the situation.

Stunt director Geeta Tandon publicly criticized the production team of Anil Kapoor's show after enduring a nine-hour wait alongside her son on set. Following her social media post detailing the disrespectful treatment, both host Anil Kapoor and guest Farah Khan issued public apologies.

facts: Geeta Tandon arrived at the shooting location at 12:30 pm on Wednesday.
She and her son left the set at 9:15 pm after waiting for nearly nine hours.
The show is hosted by Anil Kapoor.
Farah Khan appeared as a guest on the episode.
The production manager involved in the incident was named Jaydeep.

articles.headline: Ramayana Part 2 Release Pushed to 2028 as Producer Namit Malhotra Discusses Trilogy Possibilities
articles.dek: Producer Namit Malhotra has announced that the sequel to the massive epic will now arrive in 2028, while also addressing whether the franchise might expand into a trilogy.

body.h: The Schedule Change for Part Two
p: Audiences awaiting the continuation of the epic cinematic project will need to exercise additional patience. Producer Namit Malhotra recently shared that the rollout for the second installment has been shifted from its previously discussed 2027 window to a 2028 debut.

This adjustment ensures the creative teams have sufficient time to maintain production standards. The decision reflects an intentional approach to avoid rushing the creative process on such a massive undertaking.

Initially conceived as a prominent domestic project tailored for worldwide viewers, the production has expanded significantly on an international scale. The overwhelming global curiosity has inspired the team to invest extra effort into the finale.

According to the production leadership, dedicating an additional year will provide the necessary bandwidth to match the visual fidelity established in the opening chapter. Avoiding any shortcuts remains a priority for delivering a grand conclusion.

While initial planning focused on a two-part narrative structure, the overarching vision may yet adapt. The producer noted that the creative direction could expand into a three-part series depending on audience reception.

Revisiting the drawing board after the premiere of the first film allows the creators to evaluate viewer feedback carefully. Decisions regarding additions or subtractions to the storyline will rely heavily on these public responses.
The creative discussion also touches upon the presentation formats of the first installment. The team previously prepared distinct cuts featuring different runtimes for the opening chapter.
Future installments may streamline this approach based on audience reactions. The director, Nitesh Tiwari, reportedly prefers maintaining a single finalized version moving forward.
Helmed by director Nitesh Tiwari, the cinematic adaptation features a prominent ensemble cast. Ranbir Kapoor portrays Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi appears as Sita, and Yash takes on the role of Ravana.
Additional key cast members include Ravie Dubey as Lakshman and Sunny Deol as Lord Hanuman. The high-profile venture is backed by producers Yash and Namit Malhotra, operating on a substantial budget.

The monumental project has been developed on a massive budget of Rs 4,000 crore, setting a high benchmark for Indian cinema. Its theatrical rollout is scheduled to commence ahead of the festive season.
Early screenings and specialized timings, such as morning shows starting at 7 am in India, highlight the intense anticipation surrounding the arrival of the first film.
Producer Namit Malhotra revealed that the second part of the epic project will release in 2028 and hinted that the story could become a trilogy depending on audience response.
The massive production stars Ranbir Kapoor, Sai Pallavi, and Yash, and was made on a budget of Rs 4,000 crore under the direction of Nitesh Tiwari.

facts: Ramayana Part 2 release is delayed to 2028
Namit Malhotra is the producer of the film
The film was made on a budget of Rs 4,000 crore
Nitesh Tiwari is the director of Ramayana
Ranbir Kapoor stars as Lord Rama
Sai Pallavi stars as Sita
Yash stars as Ravana
Ravie Dubey stars as Lakshman
Sunny Deol stars as Lord Hanuman

articles.headline: Godzilla Minus One Climbs Digital Charts Ahead of Upcoming Sequel
articles.dek: Takashi Yamazaki’s acclaimed kaiju film is surging on streaming platforms as fans revisit the Oscar winner before the release of Godzilla Minus Zero.

p: Audiences are rapidly returning to a celebrated monster feature, pushing the title back onto prominent digital charts three years after its initial theatrical debut. Viewers have begun renting and buying the project in heavy numbers, securing it a notable placement on the iTunes Top Movies chart according to tracking data from PopVortex.

This renewed interest highlights the lasting impact of the production. Rather than fading away after its historic theatrical run, the feature continues to attract home-viewing audiences who are eager to rewatch the spectacle or experience it for the very first time.

The primary catalyst for this digital surge is the heavy anticipation surrounding the upcoming follow-up project. Studio executives officially announced the next installment, titled Godzilla Minus Zero, setting a release window for 2026.

Filmmaker Takashi Yamazaki is slated to return to helm the project, taking on writing, directing, and visual effects duties once again. Yamazaki recently shared at the Visual Effects Society Awards that scripting and storyboarding are already underway for the next chapter.

The original production was made on a modest budget of $15 million, yet it went on to achieve massive commercial success worldwide. The feature accumulated a global gross of $116 million during its theatrical exhibition.

With these impressive figures, the film officially surpassed Shin Godzilla to become the highest-grossing Japanese Godzilla movie in history. Furthermore, it claimed the record for the highest-grossing Japanese-language film ever in U.S. box office history.

The project achieved a historic milestone during awards season by capturing the Oscar for Best Visual Effects at the 96th Academy Awards. This marked a monumental moment as the first non-English language film to ever claim a victory in that specific competitive category.
The accomplishment carried even greater weight because the complex visual effects were brought to life by a remarkably small team of just 35 artists working out of Shirogumi’s Chofu studio.

Critical reception for the feature was overwhelmingly positive throughout its theatrical run. It secured an elite 99 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes derived from hundreds of professional critic reviews, alongside an enthusiastic "A" CinemaScore grade from general audiences in America.

High-profile figures also voiced their admiration for the cinematic achievement. Famed Hollywood director Steven Spielberg personally praised the work, telling Yamazaki that he watched the picture multiple times across several different formats.

Set in postwar Japan, the storyline follows a former kamikaze pilot struggling with the devastating aftermath of conflict. Ryunosuke Kamiki leads the cast in the central role, anchoring the human drama at the heart of the monster onslaught.
The film also dominated domestic award ceremonies, sweeping the 47th Japan Academy Film Prize by securing eight major honors, including the prestigious award for Best Picture.

Takashi Yamazaki’s Oscar-winning kaiju feature has experienced a major digital surge on streaming charts as fans prepare for the upcoming 2026 sequel, Godzilla Minus Zero. The original project made history with its modest budget, record-breaking global box office, and groundbreaking Academy Award win for visual effects.

facts: Takashi Yamazaki’s Godzilla Minus One is back on digital charts and sits at No. 4 on the iTunes Top Movies chart
Godzilla Minus Zero was announced by Toho on November 3, 2025, with a 2026 release window
The original film carried a reported budget of $15 million and grossed $116 million worldwide
Godzilla Minus One won Best Visual Effects at the 96th Academy Awards
The visual effects team consisted of just 35 artists at Shirogumi’s Chofu studio
The film stars Ryunosuke Kamiki as a former kamikaze pilot in postwar Japan
It earned a 99% rating on Rotten Tomatoes from 213 critics’ reviews and an “A” CinemaScore grade
The film won eight awards at the 47th Japan Academy Film Prize, including Best Picture

articles.headline: Tharun Bhascker Opens Up About Real-Life Inspiration Behind Ee Nagaraniki Emaindi Ahead of Sequel
articles.dek: Director Tharun Bhascker shares how four loyal friends inspired his cult hit Ee Nagaraniki Emaindi as he prepares for the upcoming theatrical release of the sequel ENE Repeat.

p: Filmmaker Tharun Bhascker is officially returning to the cinematic universe that captured the hearts of Telugu cinema audiences in 2018. His much-adored comedy-drama about a tight-knit gang of friends is getting a follow-up titled ENE Repeat, bringing back the signature energy that made the original picture a fan favorite over the years.

With anticipation steadily climbing ahead of its theatrical debut, the creative team has begun sharing insights into what went into crafting this continuation. Fans of the first installment have eagerly awaited further adventures of the beloved characters, and the upcoming feature aims to deliver a fresh dose of entertainment.

Reflecting on the origins of the original movie, Tharun revealed that the concept stemmed from a deeply personal place in his life. Following the massive reception of his earlier project Pelli Choopulu, the director experienced intense pressure to replicate that triumph with his subsequent artistic choices.

During a challenging phase marked by professional hurdles and professional setbacks, the filmmaker noticed a sharp shift in his social circle. While several acquaintances and relatives distanced themselves, a core group of four loyal friends chose to stand by him unconditionally through every circumstance.

The unwavering support he received from those four individuals during his lowest moments served as the foundational spark for Ee Nagaraniki Emaindi. Rather than letting the surrounding negativity define his career, he channeled those genuine bonds of brotherhood onto the silver screen.

Tharun noted that capturing authentic camaraderie felt like a natural tribute to the people who refused to abandon him. That emotional anchor resonated deeply with moviegoers, helping the 2018 release achieve a cult following long after its initial theatrical run.

Returning to this established world comes with its own unique set of obstacles, particularly regarding the high expectations harbored by dedicated fans. Tharun acknowledged that surpassing or even matching the nostalgic affection attached to the original remains his biggest competition during production.

Despite the pressure, the director maintained that the creative atmosphere on set stayed remarkably positive. He credited the collaborative spirit of the entire cast and crew for fostering an environment where creativity could thrive without creative bottlenecks.

Promising a theatrical experience filled with joy, Tharun described the upcoming sequel as a complete laugh riot that will leave audiences thoroughly entertained. He emphasized that the project was born out of positive energy that will naturally translate to the screen.

The director also added that certain sequences throughout the narrative are designed to give viewers goosebumps, blending emotional resonance with comedic timing. He views the new film as a sincere way to give back all the love fans poured into the first chapter.

ENE Repeat features the return of several key cast members from the original film alongside new additions. Vishwak Sen reprises his role as Vivek, Abhinav Gomatam steps back into the shoes of Kaushik, and Venkatesh Kakumanu returns as Uppu, while Srinath Maganti joins the main group as Karthik.

The extended ensemble cast includes Anisha Ambrose, Shivathmika Rajasekhar, Karunakumar, Priyadarshini Ram, and Mahesh Bhascker. Behind the camera, the production is guided by producers Srujan Yarabolu and Sandeep Nagireddy under SS Originals and Rootnode Cinema, featuring music by Vivek Sagar, cinematography by AJ Aaron, and editing by Raviteja Girijala.

Director Tharun Bhascker shared that the loyalty of four friends who stayed by him during past career failures inspired his 2018 film Ee Nagaraniki Emaindi. Ahead of the November 19, 2026 theatrical release of its sequel ENE Repeat, he discussed the challenges of meeting audience expectations while promising a comedy-heavy experience featuring returning stars like Vishwak Sen and Abhinav Gomatam.

facts: Tharun Bhascker directed the 2018 Telugu film Ee Nagaraniki Emaindi.
The sequel is titled ENE Repeat.
ENE Repeat is scheduled to release in theatres on November 19, 2026.

Vivek Sagar is the music composer, AJ Aaron is the cinematographer, and Raviteja Girijala is the editor.
